reviewer: AI skeptical review, not human review or native platform qualification
decision: The permanent-orphan/no-adoption policy is logically compatible with unnamed Jobs under the stated trusted-host/BFE assumptions. No removal bypass is established in the proposal itself, provided all unknown-state and live-handle requirements are actually enforced. Implementation/ABI/ACL/removal approval is withheld: the new C source/interface was absent at first inspection, and current runner/guard do not implement this authority.

logical_checks.check: Controller death and lost unnamed Job identity
logical_checks.reason: Persistent conditioned deny remains after loss of in-process handles; the helper never reopens/adopts/removes/reuses the orphan identity. Thus later inability to prove zero cannot authorize removal. This is a lifecycle design inference, not actual WFP enforcement or crash evidence.

Seal launches irreversibly, retain duplicates of actual Job/controller-created process objects, freshly require every Job ActiveProcesses0 and every retained created process signaled, then exact-key policy removal and independently queried absence. Saved state/PIDs/names are not authority.

Reserve before writes, record the real fresh profile SID, never adopt collisions or reuse any tombstoned identity, and treat torn/missing/unknown state as permanent orphan. Policy/filesystem transactions are not assumed atomic together.

BFE/host operational assumptions, no hostile administrator/kernel, no reboot/power-loss guarantee, no nonadmin product claim. Existing009 WSA10060 remains failure. The full IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP/inbound/cancellation/crash/reuse matrix is prospective, not implemented or qualified.

concrete_integration_requirements.issue: The CreateProcess-to-registration window must be covered by permanent failure state. A created suspended process can exist before assignment, and its attempted DuplicateHandle/registration itself can fail. A registered Job may therefore be empty while an unregistered process exists.
concrete_integration_requirements.required: Reserve/mark launch intent before creation or otherwise permanently poison the live guard on every failed/ambiguous creation/registration/handoff. Close/remove must refuse an unresolved launch or incomplete process registry even if later Job queries return zero. Do not let exception handling or a subsequent successful query heal this state. Retain original raw handles for the existing assigned/unassigned termination path.

concrete_integration_requirements.issue: Current finally proves immediate reaping then closes original process/Job handles; AppContainerLaunch only receives process_created/job_reaped counters. Context exit currently restores ACLs/deletes the profile when that counter is zero. Those counters or a saved cleanup_complete flag cannot authorize persistent filter removal.
concrete_integration_requirements.required: Register retained noninheritable duplicate Job/process handles through the live C owner before the relevant fallible steps. Keep duplicates through sealing, fresh zero/signaled proof and exact policy removal. Hook cleanup so any custody/query/registration error forces orphan retention; never add an unconditional filter-delete finally. Preserve current unassigned-process wait and all original cleanup errors.

concrete_integration_requirements.issue: The proposal is not evidence that four exact persistent conditioned filters, protected state/objects, source/tool identity, opaque ABI or safe removal are implemented.
concrete_integration_requirements.required: When source exists, inspect all constructors/readback/deletion paths, SID/union/buffer lifetime, native return handling and irreversible poison/seal transitions. Verify non-dynamic persistent dependencies, no zero-condition policy, exact4keys/layers/SID/action/flags/DACL, supplied keys never adopted/replaced, bounded journal writes/flush/lock/error handling, no pointer/handle authority from JSON, noninherited retained handles, host-only state/DLL and no API-error-as-absence. No build/run approval is conferred by protocol review.

concrete_integration_requirements.issue: The phrase every created process handle should distinguish controller-created suspended processes from descendants created inside an already assigned contained process.
concrete_integration_requirements.required: The controller cannot recover a child handle from a PID/JSON receipt. Retained direct-created process handles cover unassigned-launch failures; inherited no-breakaway Job membership and fresh Job zero must cover later descendants. Do not claim every descendant had an individually retained handle unless that is actually implemented and evidenced.
